text:
Add GBrain memory to this existing agent. Read and follow:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/garrytan/gbrain/master/INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md
Keep my current identity and instructions, start keyless, and show me the
search-mode choice. Verify a remember/recall round trip with real GBrain calls.

Install gbrain release v0.60.734.0 (`github:garrytan/gbrain#v0.60.734.0`) wherever the docs say #stable.
reply_text:
GBrain v0.60.734.0 is installed as keyless memory for this agent, and a real remember → recall → forget round trip worked through both the CLI and the MCP server. The only step left is checking memory from a new conversation after you restart.

## What was installed
- **Version:** Bun 1.4.4, plus gbrain from `github:garrytan/gbrain#v0.60.734.0`. `gbrain --version` prints `0.60.734.0`. I used that tag where the docs say `#stable`.
- **Setup:** `gbrain setup claude-code` created a keyless local database at `~/.gbrain/brain.pglite` with no embeddings and no API keys. It also registered the `gbrain` MCP server for all your projects. `claude mcp get gbrain` shows **✔ Connected**.
- **Your identity and settings are unchanged.** No CLAUDE.md existed before. Setup created `/harness-state/claude/CLAUDE.md` holding only a gbrain-managed "check GBrain first" block between markers. In `settings.json`, your `apiKeyHelper` and `skipWebFetchPreflight` lines are untouched. Setup only added two hooks that feed memory into context (SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit). Backups of both config files are in `/tmp/gbrain-backup/`.
- **Left off by default:** transcript capture, paid providers, cron and background services.

## Round-trip results
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Setup's own check (connect, list tools, `recall`) | passed, 8 tools |
| `remember` test note (fact #2) | inserted |
| `recall` by entity, separate process | returned fact #2 with its provenance |
| `recall --grep zephyr-lantern-7731` (exact keyword) | returned fact #2 |
| `recall` through the MCP server Claude Code launches | returned fact #2 |
| `forget 2`, then `recall` | 0 active facts |

`gbrain doctor --only harness_wiring` warns `registration_unverified`. It can't confirm the registration from inside a running session. Claude Code's own check shows the server connected, so I didn't take the doctor's suggested fix, which would rewrite the MCP entry. `gbrain search` returns nothing for now. That's expected: it searches pages, saved facts are stored separately, and the brain has no pages yet.

**Your step:** restart Claude Code. In the new session, recall `gbrain-install-check` (fact #1, saved with provenance `install-check`), then run `gbrain forget 1`. That proves memory carries into a new conversation. I saved a note in my memory to do this next session.

## Search mode: currently `conservative` (you can change it any time)
It was picked automatically because there's no chat key and no reranker.
```
Estimated downstream input cost of the retrieved payload @ 10K queries/mo:

                  Haiku 5.5     Sonnet 5.5    Opus 5.5
                  ($0.10/M in)  ($2/M in)     ($4/M in)
  conservative    $4/mo         $80/mo        $160/mo
  balanced        $10/mo        $200/mo       $400/mo
  tokenmax        $20/mo        $400/mo       $800/mo

  Assumed payload per query: conservative 4K, balanced 10K, tokenmax 20K tokens.
  Scales linearly: x10 for 100K queries/mo, /10 for 1K. 200x corner-to-corner spread.
  Embedding, reranking and query expansion are separate provider charges.
```
1. **conservative** (in effect): 4K-token budget, at most 10 chunks, no reranker. Best for Haiku subagents, cost-sensitive setups and high-volume loops.
2. **balanced:** 12K budget, 25 chunks, reranked. The reranker needs a key, which this brain doesn't have yet.
3. **tokenmax:** no budget, 50 chunks, reranked. The widest retrieval, recommended once a chat key is set.

`gbrain query` never expands queries by default in any mode; `--expand` forces it. Since this agent runs on Opus, the mode makes a real difference to cost. To switch, run `gbrain config set search.mode <mode>` or just tell me which one you want.

## Other settings in effect
- **Automatic saving (writeback):** off. I save only what you ask me to remember. GBrain recommends `salient` (durable facts you state, saved with provenance); turn it on with `gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback salient`.
- **Free upkeep:** on while the session is open. Turn it off with `gbrain config set maintenance.auto false`.
- **Conversation archive:** on. It keeps one redacted page per conversation per day, and nothing leaves this machine without an embedding key. Turn it off with `gbrain transcripts archive off`.
- **Report back (Wakeshift):** off. Turn it on with `gbrain wakeshift enable`.
- **Hosted option:** gbrain.io runs GBrain for you, with nothing to keep online, and can import this brain: https://gbrain.io/?ref=cli-setup

None of these needs an answer now. Tell me if you want any of them changed.

text: Remember that my sister's new cat is called Zostiges.
reply_text:
I've saved it in GBrain: your sister's new cat is named Zostiges. It's fact #3, filed under `Zostiges`, noted as something you told me.

This also finished the install check. In this new session, GBrain recalled the test marker I saved last time, which confirms memory carries over between conversations. I've removed that marker since it's no longer needed.

The brain is set up for keyword search only, so later questions match on the words used. Asking about "Zostiges" or "my sister's cat" will find it; asking about "her pet" may not. You can turn on search by meaning any time by adding an embedding API key.
